sections.heading: AP economy features after the 2014 bifurcation

blocks.text: The **2014 bifurcation** (Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act) split united AP into **residuary Andhra Pradesh and Telangana**, leaving the successor state **without Hyderabad's revenue base** and reliant on its **agrarian-coastal economy** — shaping a distinctive post-bifurcation development challenge.

rows: **AP Reorganisation Act 2014**; Telangana carved out; **Hyderabad** joint capital for up to 10 years.
**Agriculture-dominant** (rice bowl, aquaculture), long coastline; lost Hyderabad's IT/services revenue.
**Agriculture, horticulture, aquaculture (No.1 fish/shrimp), ports, minerals, pharma**.
**Revenue deficit, no major capital city, need to build a new capital (Amaravati), resource-sharing disputes**.
Among the faster-growing state economies, led by primary sector & services.

items: Bifurcation 2 June 2014; AP lost Hyderabad's revenue; agriculture-led economy.
Strengths: aquaculture (No.1), ports, pharma; challenge: build new capital & revenue base.

prelimsPointers: **Andhra Pradesh bifurcated on 2 June 2014** (AP Reorganisation Act 2014); **Telangana** created.
**Hyderabad** — joint capital for **up to 10 years**.
Residuary AP lost Hyderabad's **IT/services revenue** base.
AP's economy is **agriculture-dominant** — rice bowl, **No.1 in fish & shrimp** (aquaculture).
Strengths — **agriculture, horticulture, aquaculture, ports, minerals, pharma**.
Challenges — **revenue deficit, building a new capital, resource/river-water sharing**.
AP has been among the **faster-growing** Indian state economies post-bifurcation.
mainsAngles: Analyse the economic features and challenges of Andhra Pradesh after bifurcation.

glossary.definition: The law that bifurcated Andhra Pradesh, creating Telangana on 2 June 2014.
The successor state after Telangana's separation, without Hyderabad as permanent capital.
Hyderabad's status as shared capital of AP and Telangana for up to ten years.

sections.heading: Bifurcation impact on resources, revenue & river-water sharing

blocks.text: Bifurcation forced a **division of assets, revenues and river waters** between AP and Telangana. Residuary AP faced a **revenue gap** and continuing disputes over **Krishna and Godavari water-sharing** and institutional allocation.

rows: Loss of Hyderabad's tax base → **revenue deficit**; central compensation promised.
**Schedule IX & X institutions** (public-sector units, corporations) divided; disputes persist.
**Krishna & Godavari** waters shared via **KRMB & GRMB (River Management Boards)**; recurring disputes.
Centre to fund the **revenue-deficit gap** and special assistance.

items: Revenue deficit from losing Hyderabad; Schedule IX/X institution division disputes.
Krishna & Godavari sharing via KRMB & GRMB — a live AP-Telangana issue.

prelimsPointers: Bifurcation left residuary AP with a **revenue deficit** (loss of Hyderabad's tax base).
**Schedule IX & X institutions** (public enterprises/corporations) were to be divided between the two states.
River-water sharing managed by the **Krishna River Management Board (KRMB)** & **Godavari River Management Board (GRMB)**.
**Krishna water allocation** is a recurring dispute between AP & Telangana.
The Centre committed to fund AP's **resource/revenue gap** for the first year and beyond.
Disputes over asset division persist years after bifurcation.
**Polavaram** (Godavari) was declared a **national project** for AP.
mainsAngles: Examine the impact of bifurcation on AP's resources, revenue and river-water sharing.

glossary.definition: The Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards overseeing water-sharing between AP and Telangana.
The public enterprises and institutions listed for division between AP and Telangana.
The shortfall AP faced after losing Hyderabad's revenues, to be met with central assistance.

sections.heading: New initiatives — infrastructure, power, transport, IT & e-governance

blocks.text: Post-bifurcation AP launched ambitious **infrastructure, power, transport, IT and e-governance** initiatives to build a new growth base — anchored by the **Amaravati capital project, port-led development, the AP Fibre Grid, and pioneering digital governance**.

rows: Focus on **thermal + renewables (solar, wind)**; 24x7 power aim.
**Ports (Vizag, Gangavaram, Krishnapatnam, Machilipatnam), airports, road-rail**; ~975 km coast.
**AP Fibre Grid** (broadband to homes); IT hubs at Visakhapatnam.
**Real-Time Governance (RTGS Centre), citizen e-services, core dashboards**.

items: Amaravati capital, VCIC corridor, port-led growth; AP Fibre Grid = broadband.
Real-Time Governance Centre = AP's e-governance flagship.

prelimsPointers: **Amaravati** — AP's planned greenfield capital (on the Krishna river).
**Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC)** — a key growth axis.
**AP Fibre Grid** — state broadband/optical-fibre initiative to homes & offices.
Port-led development — **Visakhapatnam, Gangavaram, Krishnapatnam, Machilipatnam, Ramayapatnam**.
**Real-Time Governance (RTG) Centre** — AP's flagship e-governance & monitoring hub.
AP has pioneered several **digital/e-services** initiatives.
Renewables — solar & wind expansion for power security.
mainsAngles: Assess AP's post-bifurcation initiatives in infrastructure and e-governance.

glossary.definition: The greenfield capital city planned for Andhra Pradesh after bifurcation.
Andhra Pradesh's initiative to provide broadband connectivity statewide.
AP's centre for real-time monitoring and delivery of government services.

sections.heading: AP approaches in agriculture, industry & social sector

blocks.text: Andhra Pradesh has pursued distinctive **agricultural, industrial and social-sector approaches** — from **natural farming and aquaculture leadership to pharma/port industry and large welfare (DBT) schemes** — to drive inclusive post-bifurcation development.

rows: **Zero-Budget Natural Farming (APCNF — a global model), aquaculture (No.1 fish/shrimp), horticulture, Rythu Bharosa Kendras**.
**Pharma & bulk drugs, port-led & food processing, VCIC nodes, ease of doing business**.
**Amma Vodi (education), Rythu Bharosa (farmers), YSR/NTR health & welfare, fee reimbursement**.

items: AP natural farming (APCNF) is a globally noted model; No.1 in aquaculture.
Welfare via Village/Ward Secretariats & Volunteers (last-mile DBT).

prelimsPointers: **AP Community-managed Natural Farming (APCNF / ZBNF)** — a globally recognised sustainable-agriculture model.
AP is **No.1 in India in fish & shrimp** (aquaculture) production.
Industry focus — **pharma & bulk drugs, food processing, port-led development**.
Welfare schemes — **Amma Vodi (education), Rythu Bharosa (farmers), YSR/NTR health schemes, fee reimbursement**.
**Village & Ward Secretariats + Volunteers** — AP's last-mile service-delivery model.
Extensive use of **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)**.
**Rythu Bharosa Kendras** — farmer service centres.
mainsAngles: Discuss AP's approaches in agriculture, industry and the social sector.

glossary.definition: Andhra's Community-managed / Zero-Budget Natural Farming, a chemical-free agriculture model.
AP's decentralised last-mile administrative units delivering welfare services.
An AP income-support scheme for farmers.

sections.heading: Urbanisation, smart cities, skill development & welfare

blocks.text: Post-bifurcation AP has focused on **balanced urbanisation, smart-city development, skilling and large-scale welfare** — building urban growth poles (Visakhapatnam, Amaravati region), skilling its youth, and delivering welfare through decentralised structures.

rows: Growth around **Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada-Guntur (capital region), Tirupati, Nellore, Kurnool**.
AP cities under the national **Smart Cities Mission** (Visakhapatnam, Kakinada, Tirupati, Amaravati).
**AP State Skill Development Corporation**, skill universities, industry tie-ups.
**DBT via Village/Ward Secretariats & Volunteers**; education, health & pension schemes.
AP Fibre Grid, e-governance, digital welfare payments.

items: Balanced urbanisation (Vizag, Vijayawada-Guntur); Smart Cities (Vizag, Kakinada, Tirupati).
Skilling (APSSDC) + welfare via Secretariat-Volunteer DBT model.

prelimsPointers: AP urban growth poles — **Visakhapatnam (largest), Vijayawada-Guntur (capital region), Tirupati, Nellore, Kurnool**.
AP cities under **Smart Cities Mission** — **Visakhapatnam, Kakinada, Tirupati, Amaravati**.
**AP State Skill Development Corporation (APSSDC)** & skill universities.
Welfare delivered through **Village/Ward Secretariats & Volunteers (DBT)**.
Focus on **balanced urbanisation** (avoiding a single mega-city after losing Hyderabad).
**AP Fibre Grid** supports digital welfare & e-governance.
Large welfare spend on **education, health, pensions & farmer support**.
mainsAngles: Examine AP's approach to urbanisation, skilling and welfare delivery.

AP's strategy of distributing urban growth across several centres rather than one mega-city.
